error_chain: Wagtail Page extends AbstractPage which inherits from treebeard MP_Node, providing a materialized-path field used to encode tree position
Page.get_descendants() builds a queryset filtered by path startswith on the parent's path, expecting an index-supported prefix lookup
When the customer's custom Page subclass overrides Meta without preserving indexes, Django's options.py drops the inherited db_index for path during model construction
Django's QuerySet.filter() in db/models/query.py compiles to SQL via sql/compiler.py, which falls back to a full table scan because no usable index is registered on the path column
The query plan regression manifests as N+1 latency in Wagtail's navigation rendering despite the same source code as before
trigger_conditions: The customer's custom Page subclass overrides Meta or class_prepared without re-declaring Meta.indexes, dropping the inherited path index
Django's model-options inheritance treats Meta.indexes as non-cumulative by default; Wagtail's AbstractPage relies on the parent index being kept
The startswith path filter is only fast when the path field has a B-tree index; without it Django's compiler emits a full-scan plan

expected_answer.error_origin: Django sql/compiler.py emits a full-scan plan for the path startswith lookup because the customer's custom Page subclass dropped the inherited db_index on path
expected_answer.bypass_reason: Meta.indexes is not cumulative across abstract bases in Django's options.py; the customer's subclass silently removes Wagtail's AbstractPage.path index
expected_answer.correct_config: Re-declare Meta.indexes on the custom Page subclass to include the path B-tree index, or leave Meta unset so Wagtail's AbstractPage Meta is inherited verbatim
